Sara, Vanessa — adding technical detail so procurement can map to existing chargebacks: 

1) Ingest vs storage:
   - Ingest (charged): spans processed by the runtime are metered per 1M spans. This covers compute for indexing, linking to KV caches, and short-term hot storage used for queries under 24–72 hours.
   - Storage (charged): GB-month for trace retention beyond the hot window. Longer retention tiers (3/6/12 months) are GB-month-prorated.

2) Seatless model:
   - Dashboard units are priced in slabs (0–50u / 51–250u / 251+). Each dashboard unit represents expected concurrent dashboard render capacity — it's not a user seat.
   - Dashboards that require advanced widgets (live token-level tracing) count as 2 units each for tiering.

3) Sampling & cost control:
   - You can apply dynamic sampling rules per environment; sampled spans still incur ingest cost but may reduce indexed storage.
   - We recommend prefix-level KV caching for high-volume endpoints to drop redundant spans before indexing.

Commercial concession we can offer for StratusBank:
   - 12-month commit: 20% off the observability add-on SKU + waived onboarding fee.
   - 3-month pilot (no long-term commit): 10% off for first quarter, then revert to list or enter a commit.
   - If you commit to both Dedicated capacity and a 12-month observability commit, we can add a $25k credit applicable against overages for the first two quarters.

I attached an example calculation in the XLS (sheets: ingest_workflow, retention_examples) showing per-span and per-GB math for your sample.

Happy to walk the team through a short call — I can show how sampling and dashboard units move the needle on cost.
